correctness.rationale: For each nontrivial subgroup, barycentric invariance identifies geometric fixed points exactly with a coset-orbit complex. All cosets are admissible iff the subgroup contains only weight-one or weight-two nonzero vectors at scale two. Complete classification of binary rank-two diameter-two subspaces gives coordinate squares and even-parity triples; every larger subspace is ruled out. Explicit maximum-distance calculations yield Q_{n-1} graphs for weight-one/two involutions and isolated coset vertices for admissible rank-two subgroups; the inclusion at scale one is their zero-skeleton. The explicit binary basis change proves the graph isomorphism, and V/E counts give the integral homotopy type. Packaged finite exhaustive subgroup enumerator corroborates n=3,4,5,6 without substituting for proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies every nontrivial translation-subgroup fixed-point space and its small-scale filtration for the entire family of binary Hamming cubes, with two different nontrivial isotropy ranks and exponential integral circle multiplicities. It gives the equivariant fixed-space diagram at the first nontrivial scales, information finer than the previously classified parent wedge-of-three-spheres and its characteristic-zero homology character. The square and even-parity triple subgroups supply an exact nontrivial isotropy boundary, not a routine numerical increment.
